title: selfdoc.py and backlog.py usage errors are measured from this host's transcripts and the top ones fixed at the tool
goal: python3 _tools/kbusage.py errors [--days N] prints, from the local Claude Code transcripts of this clone's project only and storing nothing, the first line of each failed Bash call of a _tools/ script grouped by script and normalised message (paths, ids and numbers replaced by placeholders), with counts, most frequent first, so a usage error that agents repeat is seen once; selfdoc.py section DOC with no heading prints the doc's headings with their line ranges and exits 0 instead of argparse's usage error; the three most frequent backlog.py and selfdoc.py messages the report shows on 2026-W41 transcripts are each fixed at the tool (a default, a clearer refusal naming the flag to use, or an accepted form) in this story's commits; the week after, querylog.py digest shows call.tool errors of tools.selfdoc and tools.backlog each under one in twenty of their calls.

gates.question: Which of the report's messages rank for the three fixes: the usage errors only (exit 2, the tools' bad-arguments and refusal code) or every failed call (exit 1 too)?
options: exit 2 only: usage errors and refusals; exit 1 lines are gate verdicts (done reasons, selfdoc stale, selfcheck) a tool fix would hide
every exit: the raw ranking, done's not-done line and selfdoc stale lines first
gates.recommendation: exit 2 only: usage errors and refusals; exit 1 lines are gate verdicts (done reasons, selfdoc stale, selfcheck) a tool fix would hide

notes: Premise (digest 2026-W41 and the ops sidecars since 2026-10-05): call.tool errors tools.selfdoc 70 of 369 calls (19 in 100), tools.backlog 133 of 1973 (7 in 100), python-c 50 of 428; call.tool rows hold the class and outcome only, never the message, so the message must be read from the transcripts on the host that made them (kbusage already reads a prompt's transcript; kb/_self/usage.md). The report is a local read like backlog.py cost --rework: nothing is written to the spool or the store, and a message is printed normalised, never a command line. One usage error seen in this session: 'selfdoc.py section maintaining' without a heading exits 2 with 'section takes DOC HEADING pairs'. The new read-only command gets its Bash(...) and PowerShell(...) allow rules in .claude/settings.json and a check that it refuses a transcript path outside the Claude config directory of this user, per the plan rule for read-only commands. The three backlog.py fixes are chosen from the report, not guessed: a fix the report does not rank in the top three is out of scope. Precheck 2026-10-08: selfdoc.py section maintaining exits 2 and kbusage.py errors --days 7 has no such command, so two of three checks fail until the work is done; test_check_programs.py passes before and pins the allow-rule check for the new read-only command.
